Great place to have a coffee or other drink like matcha latte. They also sell coffee beans and some merchandise. Loved the outdoor seating and view of the sea from the balcony upstairs. The almond blueberry cake was to die for!!

This is a must come place. Coffee is great as are the snacks and other drinks. This cafe is comparable to the ones I have been in Singapore, Hong Kong and New York. There are also attractive souvenirs to be purchased. Air-conditioning is cool and nice music is being placed.

One of the best coffees I’ve ever had. Such a good vibe inside, and definitely a must visit place. Buying coffee here to bring as souvenirs is probably the best thing someone could do, and it’s quite affordable.

The coffee is strong and dark chocolate-like. It's really delicious. The atmosphere is unlike anything you'd find in East Timor. But there's a strange system. They don't accept credit cards, only bank transfers or cash. Plus, for $40, they only give you one shopping bag. Even if you spend $100, they only give you one. So, you have to ask them to split the bill. For $100, they might give you two, but they don't.
Long black is strong with 4 shots, and latte is only 1 shot because the milk doesn't taste good. I don't really... recommend it.

Worthwhile if you have a scooter or transport. Nice break from tye city. Park up top and walk down to the left. Normal gravel off street parking. More of a cafe than a museum but beautiful vista. Starlink wifi for customers (password on a chalkboard from 2019).

I am biased as I am timorese and love history, however the place is pretty run down, no signage and without people like me to suggest friends and colleagues visiting Timor to come and see it, few people would visit. I understand it may be hard to people living nearby to keep this place up and running on a volunteer basis, I would love to contribute and redo/re print the panels, However I do not know who is managing this, but what I came to know it that the place is closed on Saturday and Sunday, which I was not aware off nor did I see any signs, I opened the door the panels were there, went with some visitors in wanted to leave the usual contributions, did not see anybody, no signing book or collection box, 15 minutes after got a very angry Auntie, saying that the place was closed. I explained I did not know as there was no sign, the door was not locked, the only door locked was to door granting access to the restaurant. Despite me best efforts to say sorry in both tetun and Portuguese

What a gorgeous little Cafe with the ability to learn some very important history. The Coffee and Iced Chocolate were both amazing!! A nice drive, the road there was fine on a scooter, all bitumen with very little holes.

Dare Memorial Museum & Café is located in the hills above Díli about a 30-minute drive from the city center. We can enjoy stunning views over Díli, the coastline, and nearby hills with a Timorese coffee, fresh juice, sandwiches, pizza, and light refreshments like toast and chips.
Nice place to see the the bay of Dili from 500m up the mountain. Good milkshakes and pizza. Allow some time, service can be slow in case there are other customers. Open from 9AM to 9PM.

(04/2025) Although this place carries a powerful idea, it feels strange and run-down. Parking is difficult, the informational posters are faded, and the museum is in poor condition — there’s no actual monument on site. Instead, there’s an oddly oversized café with bland coffee and uninterested staff, playing classical music from the speakers. Wi-Fi is password-protected and not available to guests. However, the view from here is absolutely stunning.

This more like a cafe and photo spot.
I didn’t feel like a museum at all.
Good view and location.
Takes forever to get my order, wait one and half an hour to get my juice, but they end up bring wrong order, even though it wasn't a  busy day.

A small yet informative museum just outside of downtown Dili. There is a coffee shop located at the museum as well. Great place to visit to immerse in the culture and history of East Timor. Beautiful view of downtown Dili and the beach as well.

the drive on a bike isn’t bad but there’s a few nasty potholes that will end your day; don’t speed. once there, as with most places in dili, not great signage. it’ll be on your right as you get to a 3 way fork with a small white sign. park in the lot and then take the stairs going down in the corner. walking down some steps and mazes to get the “museum” and cafe. Great view and even tho the museum is only like 5 banners the info is very good. limited menu but my sandwich was good. bathrooms clean. limited English at restaurant but service friendly and fast. they won’t accept $1 paper bills.

I'm not sure why people complain about the drive up to Dare.  Look at a map. It shows it's a twisty mountain road.
The view of Dili is one of the best I have found.

Quick drive or grueling bike ride from Dili. Awesome spot to learn more about the history of Timor Leste and enjoy a coffee and toasty!
Pizzas taste amazing and so well priced. 2wD road to get here very accessible and well worth the views and cooler climate. Highly recommend

A true hidden Gem near Dili! The Cappuccino was just as it should be and the Views are amazing. You can see all over Dili from here. They have a lot of spaces and you'll also get some History lessons in the entrance area. The Terrace is really beautiful. Would highly recommend.

Even at the weekends it is quiet and relaxing, with jazz music playing, and plenty of seating and a fair number of parks. There is also an informative memorial to the fighting in Timor during WW2

This small archive right opposite the resistance museum offers a short documentary about Max Stahl and his work during and after the resistance. You'll see some interview parts, and some scenes Max filmed during the times of resistance including the massacre. The man who showed me the movie was very nice and open to questions.

Opposite the Timorese Resistance Archive & Museum, this is an institution dedicated to preserving the audiovisual history of Timor-Leste, and providing educational opportunities. Inside you are likely to find young Timorese using the facilities, and you can watch footage of the Santa Cruz Massacre filmed by British journalist Max Stahl.
Audiovisual Archive Localhost
Really cool traditional tais exhibit and mini museum inside this complex! Learn about the history and art of this beautiful country! Not sure the hours of operation but worth checking out for sure.

We have used Manny Timor Tours many times for our groups. Whether it is 30 people or an individual, Manny and his team are professional, knowledgeable and amazing

Manny can create the perfect itinerary you and help you with transport, accommodation and food recommendations

As an Australian based Travel Agent (Darwin) I have specialised in Timor-Leste for almost 8 years and throughout that time my go to tour operator has been Manny Timor Tours. The whole team is passionate, knowledgeable and attentive to all my clients  needs. They make their experiences so much better by providing the local personal touch. Highly recommend using Manny Timor Tours.

I have had the pleasure of taking seven trips in Timor with Manny Napoleon and his drivers over 11 years.  Five trips with students and two with friends. Manny is reliable knowledgeable organised friendly and his drivers are fantastic. We visit more remote areas where the roads are 4 WD only and the drivers handle the conditions with skill care and good humour. They are excellent company and end up being friends. I look forward to many more tours with Manny!

Three of us revisited some old haunts from 1999. We travelled to Dili, Batugade, Balibo, Maliana, Bobonaro, Suai, Ainaro, Maubisse, Aileau and Baucau by 4WD. Our driver and Guide - Serafim - was terrific! He had great driving skills and was able to tell us a lot about the country, its history and its people. We changed our itinerary as we travelled, and the head office was able to make changes for us quickly and easily. We would highly recommend Manny Timor Tours.

We had a fantastic trip. Alex was such a great guide. He was able to tweak the schedule to our needs and was great with our kids. He so generously shared his personal experiences of the Timor liberation, the feeling he described will stay with us for a long time. We will tell anyone who listens to come and visit Dili and use this service. It added a depth of meaning to our trip that I don’t think you could find in just wandering about. We are so grateful that we could learn from Alex and have him share his knowledge with us.

An Unforgettable Day Trip to Balibó
Manny Tours Timor delivered an absolutely outstanding full-day experience to Balibó a place of profound historical significance as the site where the Balibo Five were tragically murdered. It’s a sobering and deeply moving destination, and having a knowledgeable guide made all the difference in understanding the weight of what happened there.
Fair warning to anyone booking this tour: the road to Balibó is rough, with extensive roadworks along the way, so be prepared for a bumpy ride. That said, it’s absolutely worth every pothole. The journey itself is part of the adventure, offering incredible scenery through the Timorese countryside.
A highlight we didn’t expect was a visit to the Indonesian border, which added a fascinating geopolitical dimension to the day and really put the history of the region into context.
A special mention must go to our guide Jonias, who was exceptional knowledgeable, passionate about the history of Timor-Leste, and a genuin

We chose this company during our recent trip to Timor Leste from 17-20 Mar 2026. Our driver, Serafim really knowledgeable and fun person to bring us around with some unlocking discovery site and highly recommended to anyone who wants to Future. If want to visit to Timor Leste please choose Manny Timor Tours as this company can give you maximum experience overall.

Obrigado Manny

I did a 1 day tour to see the countryside. I wanted to try some local foods and coffee. My driver was Luis and he was great. Was able to tell me a lot about the area and the history. They arranged pick up and drop off at the hotel. Highly recommend to get outside of Dili and see all that Timor Leste has to offer.

What a great experience with Afonso. He was so kind, knowledgeable, and adapted to our needs and interest well. We had a very short stay in Dilli but we managed to hit the museum, Jesus Rei, the mall, and Afonso helped arrange a donation at a convent orphanage for disabled children. The car was solid and Afonso was always a bit early waiting for us calmly. The setup and communication was excellent and everything went off without an issue. Thank you!

Had the best tour with Lito today! I only had a short amount of time, so he tailored the day perfectly to make sure I got to see all the highlights. He had the answers to all of my questions and made me feel so comfortable and safe (solo female traveller). When I come back to Timor I will definately be booking with this company and will be requesting Lito as my guide again! Thank you Lito for the best day!

A few years ago I wrote a book about the trials and tribulations of the Dutch colonial army of the former Dutch East Indies (KNIL) and the Australian commandos against the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII on Timor. This was requested by daughters and sons of these Dutch (which includes many people with Indonesian roots) veterans. A friend of mine persuaded me to visit Timor and all these places. So we went this summer, for which I'm very grateful to him. But where to start? This certain part of history was all so very specific. Manny Timor Tours was the only company that made a specific itinerary about WWII (including the lesser known Dutch participation) on the entire island of Timor. And it was also their first time - my compliments.

We had Serafim as our guide, a very nice and accessible man that really made our trip. He knows six forms of Tetum and endlessly translated for us, which truly enhanced our experience of the history of Timor, having many conversations with elderly Tim

We did a 14 day tour from Timor-Leste to West-Timor. Started in Dìli, Ataúro, Mount Ramelau, Suai, Samé, Loihuno, Tutuàla, Jaco Island, Baucau, Liquica, Balibó, Atambua, Soé, Kupang. In Timor-Leste our guide and driver Serafim really went out of his way to give us the best experience. He was also a great travelling companion, translated a lot of stories of local Timorese and told us a lot about the country by his own experience. We fell in love with the beautiful nature and had a great time with the people. What really stood out in the tour that we also saw the difficult history of Timor-Leste (colonial times, WO II and Indonesian time). This gave the full picture. Our time in West-Timor was also very nice, beautiful nature and very interestering to learn more about the culture.

The 4x4 drive car in Timor-Leste was necessary and very comfortable. Serafim is a good driver. In addition, accommodations are in line with booking, can be basic in more rural areas, but this was expected.

3 Puerto Ricans girls ready to explore the undiscovered. We came to Timor Leste without any expectations and left in love with this young country. We did a 4 day tour including a hike to Mt Remalau. Everything was arranged for us. Highly recommend 💯 this company to tour Timor Leste. Obrigado

Had the pleasure of joining a half-day tour with Manny on a work trip.

An excellent experience—Manny shared extensive local knowledge and kept us laughing the whole time. You’re in very good hands with this team!

Alex our tour guide was an amazing host and representative of Timor Leste. We booked a private tour to Balibo and Alex took us to several other historical sight, shared all his knowledge and was so kind. We will be doing another tour to Baucau and Manatuto where my son is a Peace Corp volunteer. I highly recommend supporting the local community here.

Had an incredible all day tour with Serafin. We saw the highlights of Dili including Cristo Reí (make sure you bring plenty of water), the resistance museum and more. Serafin really went out of his way so we could enjoy the absolute most out of our trip (including a delicious coffee break). Im very thankful I decided to book with these guys. Highly recommend. Thanks guys! See you next time :)

Manny Timor tours was great. I booked a 3 day, 3 night tour and they handled everything. My guide/driver Serafim was with me the whole time and he was great. I couldn’t recommend him and the travel agency more.

My girlfriend and I booked a half day tour around Dili, and we enjoyed it a lot. Manny, our driver and guide made it fun for us, and gave us a lot of great information about the country. The communication while organizing the tour was perfect as well.

We did a four day tour booked through gateway travel with Manny Timor Tours. Everything was arranged for us but they were very flexible with what we wanted to do- a mix between some beach/ snorkelling time and also some historical information/ museums and markets. They even got up early for us one morning to do a sunrise walk up Cristo Rei at our request.

The highlight of the trip was a day tour to Balibo with lunch at the forte and a walking tour of the local village. The roads there were a bit rough in places but felt very safe in a 4WD with Lito as our experienced local driver.

On an Atauro island day trip a local guide, Erni, came with us to help find snorkelling gear/ lunch/ transport on the island itself.

Could not recommend Manny Tours more highly as a local business who are very knowledgeable about Timorese history and culture, and how to get the most out of your time there.

We had a very enjoyable experience in Timor Leste thanks' to Manny Timor Tours. Our 14 day holiday was very well co ordinated from the day we arrived at the airport to our departure 14 days later.  We very much got a cultural experience thanks to our wonderful guide Serafin who was also our driver and companion. The itinerary basically covered all parts of Timor Leste along the coat and into the mountains and a few days on the nearby  Atauro Island. Wed like again to thank Manny and his team and would have no hesitation in highly recommending Manny Timor Tours  if your considering visiting and experiencing this amazing country and its people and places. Angelo & Mara.

I just finished an incredible tour to Maubessi that I can't recommend enough! The landscapes were breathtaking, and the activities were well-planned and enjoyable. One of the best parts was visiting traditional houses and interacting with the locals, who were all so friendly. I even got to try some homemade coffee, which was absolutely delicious!

The transportation was modern and comfortable, making the journey a pleasure. My guide, Serefim, was fantastic! He was not only friendly but also shared fascinating insights about the culture and history of the area. He made sure to stop at all the key highlights and captured some beautiful photos along the way.

As a solo traveler, I felt completely at ease and thoroughly enjoyed every moment of the tour. If you're considering this experience, go for it! You won't be disappointed!

I spent ten days on a tour with Manny Timor Tours. It first started by contacting the agency  to customise the tour. Lito, and then Erin, were very responsive and helpful. In the end, we decided to take bits and pieces of existing packages and ended up with a tour starting from Dili, going the to Mount Ramelau, Suai in the Southern Coast, Same, Betano, Viqueque, Ossù, Mondo Perdido, Veniliale, Baucau, Los Palos, Tutuala, Jaco Island, Com and then back to Dili through Baucau. This tour was a good mix between hiking, including the ascent of Mount Ramelau to see the wonderful sunrise, beach activities, and history, from the Portuguese colony to the Japanese attacks during WWII and, more recently, the massacres related to the Indonesian occupation.

Alex, my guide was very friendly and knowledgeable, particularly of the history during the occupation times. In addition to fully following the programme, he also sometimes went for the extra-mile, for example when we visited one of his friends

I highly recommend Manny Timor Tours. They were very professional, friendly, well organised and reliable. We were a family group of ten (four adults, four kids, two older adults), and they were flexible with our needs (we had a full day tour of Dili and another day up to Maubisse and Aileu). They accomodated extra stops we asked to make, and when we needed transport into the evening in Dili, they arranged for the driver to stay on for a small fee.

Lito (aka Manny), Carmen, Alex and Joko were all a pleasure to interact with. And Erni looks after bookings. Can't say enough good things about them.

Alex was awesome and showed us all the cool spots. He shared his personal experience with the war in Timor and was very open and generous. Our flight was delayed and he spent an extra hour showing us the city. Thank you Alex!

Spent a lovely afternoon with Lito, he was keen to show us around and we packed in a lot. It was a very relaxed yet engaging approach and we appreciated that. Interesting to learn about a new country in this manner.

Great tour agency who provided a customized 5-day tour to see the highlights of this beautiful country!

Dalam perjalanan kami dari PLBN Motaain ke Dili, kami melintasi salah satu tempat menarik dan bersejarah, Ai Pelo Prison. Kala itu 2022-Jun, kami mampir melihat sisa/ reruntuhan bangunan di pinggir pantai. Salah satu jejak sejarah Portugis di Pulau Timor, khususnya di Negara Timor Leste. Tak banyak informasi di bagunan tersebut kala itu. Pemandangan dari atas dengan garis pantai yang panjang, keren. Jadi kalau ke Timor Leste, Ai Pelo Prison bisa sebagai salah tujuan untuk wisata sejarah. Terima kasih.

The locked gate didn’t help much because the wall and the gate itself are low enough to climb over.
Anyway the guard saw me and came to open the gate. He was kind and explained a basic information about the place.
After the visit he asked me to sign a visitor book. He didn’t ask for any fee but I gave him a small change for his help.

Unfortunately, the informational signage is faded to the point that much of it is unreadable. It's a fine place to stop for a few minutes, but the lack of historical context due the faded signage made the visit underwhelming. Hopefully the $1 entrance fee will be put towards updating this in the future.

Informative boards with the history of the Aipelo Prison, in three languages, Tetum, Portuguese, and English.  Very interesting history.
The stone walls are all still standing after around 100 years.
There were toilets and a first aid room, a recent addition, but they were locked.
It's definitely worth stopping at if you're driving past or as part of many sites on the trip between Dili and Balibo if you're interested in the history of Timor Leste.
Mandatory stopping point on the trip, because it's Interesting place to learn about the history of the prison and the Portuguese presence in TL.

Definitely worth stopping to visit if you're driving through Ai Pelo. The signage is some of the best I've come across in Timor-Leste (usually there is none!). Atmospheric and relatively well preserved former Portuguese prison in use between 1889 and 1939
Interesting historical site! Decent signage too. Definitely worth stopping at if driving by, and or a short trip from Dili!

Dilapidated remains of Portuguese built Administrative Headquarters cum prison was in service until 1939. Located about 12 kms west of Dili city on the highway to Liquica. Good spot for doing a quick photography. But no restaurant or rest rooms available in the vicinity.
Don't make a special trip but if you are in the area its worth a quick look. Old prison and Fort from Portuguese colonisation. Used to stop smugglers.
We can learn about the history that Dr. Jose Ramos Horta, current President of Timor Leste, made through his life.

Additionally, visitors can also see all the awards, and honorary degrees conferred upon him, as well as other memorabilia. It is one of the few venues that can be visited for free

During our collaboration for the Malaysia Expo Dili 2025, we were warmly welcomed by the friendly staff, who generously allowed us to capture photographs celebrating both Timorese and Malaysian cultures.

Their support made our experience not only enjoyable but also inspiring. This museum is a must-visit for anyone interested in the vibrant heritage of Timor-Leste.

Museum tentang perjuangan rakyat Timor-Leste meraih kemerdekaan. Dari era penjajahan Portugis hingga pendudukan Indonesia. Wajib dikunjungi kalau mau belajar sejarah, utamanya hal-hal yang tidak akan diajarkan di sekolah-sekolah di Indonesia.

Saya jadi paham dan memang selayaknya Timor-Leste menjadi negara sendiri dan bukan bagian dari Indonesia.

Museum ini lebih banyak berupa ilustrasi dan teks narasi, dibandingkan benda-benda bernilai historis. Teks dalam 3 bahasa: Tetum, Portugis dan Inggris. Sayangnya tata letak teks bahasa Inggrisnya kurang nyaman, jadi kalau mau membaca kadang harus sambil jongkok atau duduk di lantai.

Ada perpustakaan juga tentang Sejarah timor leste, perjuangannya, maupun tentang Timor-Leste sebagai negara baru.

Sebenarnya ada aturan tidak boleh mengabil foto di dalam Museum, tp saya diam2 ambil foto hehehehe.

One of the best museums I have ever been to. The details discussed are really minute and it is shocking to have such a detailed retelling of the atrocities which made this place miserable in the past. It is definitely a place to go to immerse oneself in the local history and to feel the agony of the people.

The $5 entry fee for foreigners is well worth it. I learned so much.  The displays are informative and everything is written in English, Portuguese and Tetum. The staff are friendly and happy to give extraterrestrial information about the displays

A museum you must visit when you come to Timor-Leste.
When we talk about genocide, our minds often jump straight to Europe. But traveling through Southeast Asia, I’ve repeatedly come across stories of occupation and genocide from the eastern side of the world—stories that are just as brutal, just as important, and far less spoken about.
Timor-Leste is a newly independent Asian nation that lived through decades of occupation under different regimes. The trauma here runs deep—woven through families, carried across generations. This museum stands as a quiet but powerful reminder of the ugly reality of colonialism, war, and genocide.
What makes the experience truly human, though, are the guides.

The first fine arts school, cultural center and artists’ association in Timor-Leste, established in 2003. It gained an international reputation for its varied, and often surreal, art incorporating Timorese culture and motifs. In December 2021 it was controversially evicted from its home in the former National Museum in Comoro, which had been promised by the then government to veterans. Thankfully it found a new home in the former air traffic control tower of the original Dili airport, located to the south of Nicolau Lobato Presidential Palace. Bit tricky to find but I'm sure people could point the way if you made some sufficient bat-like gestures. My friend is a professional guide and told me this is the only such bat colony in Timor-Leste. The bats seem pretty similar to those found in Australia, no doubt related to them, but I noticed that unlike colonies in Australia these ones didn't smell. Maubisse is full of history to learn and study. 2018 I was filming Timor Awakening 7, Australian War Veteran group was travelling with Ian Hampel, WW2 Commando who was observing Japanese movements 1942 all over Timor-Leste. Amazing story of hardship and survival. I was honoured to spend time with this amazing person. His memories were sharp as knife. Large group of TA7 group was following the paths Ian Hampel walked through Timor-Leste. Postu Maubisse was strategically important spot for Japanese and they stationed lots of troops there. Australian Commandos were observing their movements from the surrounding hills and relayed the information to Australia. Many fights occurred in this area and Commandos disappeared to the mountains with the help of Timorese. Japanese never catched these "White Ghosts".

"Larigutu Viqueque Ossu" refers to locations within the Viqueque Municipality of Timor-Leste, specifically highlighting Larigutu and Ossu, which are administrative areas within the larger Viqueque region.
Here's a breakdown of what the information indicates about these places:
Viqueque Municipality:
* Location: Located in the southeast of Timor-Leste, about 183 km from Dili, the capital. It borders Lautém (east), the Timor Sea (south), Manatuto (west), and Baucau (north).
* Administrative Posts: It comprises five administrative posts: Lacluta, Ossu, Uatu-Lari (also known as Leça or Watulari), Uatu-Carbau (Watucarbau), and Viqueque, which collectively contain 36 villages (sucos).
* History: Viqueque had traditional authority before Portuguese rule. The Portuguese established their office in 1698 and in 1859, Viqueque became a district known as Bibiluto District. It was a district during the Indonesian occupation and became a municipality after independence.

Ili Kere Kere is reached by a rough road off the main road between Tutuala and Valu Beach, followed by a 2.3km return walk (not the 250m denoted by the signage at the start of the trail). This walk gets increasingly rough and steep (downhill) before reaching the best known rock art depicting a sea urchin, as well as a harder to recognise image of cockfighting. Walking around the base of the cliff offers great views of Jaco Island in the distance. Allow about an hour to visit Ili Kere Kere. Look out for the giant bee hives hanging from the rock overhang above the rock art.

From where the trail to Ili Kere Kere starts there are two other trails that are far less visited. Pati-Patinu (500m walk apparently) goes to seven holes in stone, which demonstrate a tradition practice by ancestors of the Tutuala area

Mundu Perdido, meaning "Lost World" in Portuguese, is a significant mountain and a protected area located in the Viqueque District of Timor-Leste, specifically to the west of the town of Ossu.
Here's a detailed explanation:
Name Origin: The name "Mundu Perdido" comes from the Portuguese, likely given because the mountain is frequently shrouded in mist and clouds, making it appear as if it's hidden or "lost." This phenomenon is common for many mountains in Timor-Leste during much of the year.
Fatin Furak

The landscapes of Mundo Perdido ("Lost World" in Portuguese) are varied and atmospheric places to explore on foot. The Portuguese called it the Lost World as the area is so often hidden in mist. The best time of year to visit to try and get views is between August and October. The area was an important hideout for Timorese independence fighters during the Indonesian occupation. Now it is designated an ‘Important Bird Area’, home to 63 different species, and is one of the three most important areas for orchids in Timor-Leste. There are no clear trails and getting lost is easily done, so a local guide is strongly recommended. A couple of options are Joni on +670 7727 7996 or M.Xisto on +670 7604 1207. Two popular places to start hiking from are about 45 minutes drive (on a challenging road) to the west of Larigutu and from close to Ossu.

Discover Rai Mutin (White Land), one of Timor-Leste's geological wonders. This unique landscape features expansive areas of exposed white limestone, created by the weathering of the rock's top surface. The result is a striking, foreign environment that contrasts dramatically with the surrounding green hills.

While several areas of 'white land' can be found throughout the Aileu district, this particular site is one of the most prominent and accessible formations. Located just a 15-minute drive from Aileu's main town, Rai Mutin Limestone Park offers a free-to-enter natural experience. It's an ideal spot for photography, a short walk, or simply to appreciate a quieter side of Aileu.

review_text: When the mist comes in, the Balibo Fort Hotel seems to float in the clouds.  It reminds me of the Cameron Highlands in the 1960’s when there was no pollution and a trip to the mountain resort was the perfect place to get away from the tropical heat. Built as a Fort 400 years ago by the Portuguese, the original stone walls, entry archway and cannons are still there. Please support the locals by buying their local honey. Inquire with villagers to find out how you can buy a jar of this sweet product directly from the source.

A Hidden Historical Gem in Timor-Leste

Maubara Fort is a fascinating piece of Timor-Leste’s history. Perched on a hill, it offers stunning views of the surrounding landscape and the sea. The fort itself, though small, is well-preserved and gives a real sense of the colonial past. Walking around, you can imagine the strategic importance it once had. It’s a peaceful spot, perfect for history lovers and photographers alike. A must-visit for anyone exploring the western part of Timor-Leste!

The old Duth fortifications stand silent under a grand canopy of old trees. The shade was welcome after a morning in the car, in late Spring heat.
Our guide took us up to the the remaining building, which is now a small cafe and a souvenir shop of handmade crafts.
The cafe offered a tamarind drink, which was wonderfully sour, offset with lemonade. Perfect!
There are a few old canons still in place, inviting a wealth of stories from our guide.
Opposite this site are more craft shops, with an impressive selection of local fabrics (Tais).

review_text: On 31 August 1942 Aileu was invaded by Colunas Negras, the Timorese allies of the Japanese invaders. review_text: Great for adventure seekers who want to get away from it all. One of Timor Leste’s two islands (with Atauro Island), Jaco is an uninhabited, 10km2 island about 700m off the eastern end of mainland Timor-Leste, home to beautifully clear waters off a white sand beach. There isn’t really anything on the island, other than an impressive set of whale bones to the south of where the boats land, and a thick bush interior with no paths, but it is a quiet and relaxing place. Just off shore are several patches of coral, though less diverse or life filled than those around Atauro Island, and with stronger currents. It isn’t possible to hire snorkel gear locally so bring it with you. There are a surprising number of deer, given that there is no reliable fresh water supply on the island. It is an important site for birds, including rare birds such as the great cuckoo dove and the orpheus fathead. Jaco Island is considered sacred by Timorese and staying overnight is not allowed, but it is a popular place to visit for a few hours.

Walking into Timor Plaza today, I see a modern building with glass elevators and bright lights. It feels like any shopping mall you would find in other Asian cities. But this place carries a heavy story. It opened in October 2011 as the first modern shopping center in Timor-Leste. It was built by the Jape Group, a family business started by Jape Kong Su, a man born in Balibo who fled the country in 1975 and built his fortune in Darwin, Australia. He returned in 1999 to help rebuild his homeland, and this mall became his biggest project.

Today, the place is busy. The Jape family says more than 3,000 people work in the Dili Central compound every day, directly or indirectly. The mall has a supermarket, banks, phone companies, restaurants, and the only cinema in the country. There is even a free medical clinic run by the Order of Malta. For many Timorese, it is a place to find work, buy goods, or watch a movie. For others, it is a symbol that their country is moving forward.

The mixture looks like Malaysian popiah filling but it tastes so incredibly amazing - earthy and subtle flavor of the grated cassava, cassava leaves, papaya flower. I could eat so so much of this, it's healthy too! Tastes a bit of the daun ubi of the Orang Ulu in Sarawak and the cassava leaves soup of the Rwandans - the kind of food foraged from the forest. 😍😍😍

Topped with a savory, sweet, tangy pork belly stew, something like a Filipino pork adobo. Like seriously damn freaking good with the cassava mix.

I was on a quest today to find authentic Timorese cuisine prior to the Portuguese and Indonesian influences. Found this gem, operated by young Timorese entrepreneurs, with a passion for preserving culture and food heritage while also introducing visitors to their cuisine. Ahi matan translates to "the source of the fire." I had such a nice time talking to them, and of course, the food was delicious. I ordered the flatbread made from purple sweet potatoes (which are abundant here), a stew (batar fai) made of grilled corn, red bean, peanuts, moringa leaves, and served with a side of chili-rubbed rosella leaves. The stew was served with a side of tofu and green beans in a rich turmeric sauce and fresh veggie salad with stewed spinach. I washed it all down with a cold glass of soursop ginger juice. I will be returning here again and again.

Forte da Baguia foi um forte Português construído na cidade de Baguia, Baucau,Timor-Leste, durante o governo de José Celestino da Silva (1894 – 1908).

O forte foi construído com um muro de duas camadas, sendo uma externa e a outra interna que o envolve no formato de um retângulo no qual existem três edifícios ao todo. Nos cantos da parede há duas torres e entre elas uma abertura. Envolvendo a parede interna há mais um muro de defesa, que utiliza a encosta como proteção adicional e também uma ponte sobre um fosso na sua frente.

Durante a rebelião de Viqueque, no início de junho de 1959, os insurgentes tentaram tomar o forte.eles contavam com pelo menos cem rebeldes, no entanto, foram repelidos por soldados profissionais, que contavam com um uso mais efetivo dos equipamentos bélicos e também tinham uma metralhadora como aliada. Esta tentativa fracassada de tomar o forte resultou em destruição de grande parte do forte.

O forte foi reinaugurado em 2014, na sua cerimonia de reinauguração

Foodie Critique: Joyful Restaurant (Timor Plaza)

Stopped by this Hong Kong–style restaurant around noon. With only two guests in the dining room—including myself—I expected at least a smile or a welcome. Instead, there was silence and stares. Even getting a menu required me to ask, which set the tone for the meal.

I had come looking forward to a proper Hong Kong–style milk tea, but surprisingly it wasn’t available. Only bubble tea was offered, which I declined. For a restaurant positioned as HK-style, not having this basic staple is a gap.

I ordered the Bitter Melon Beef Rice. Unfortunately, the beef was overly salty, and the bitter melon lacked balance. The only part I can compliment was the plain white rice, which at least helped tone down the saltiness of the dish.

Reflections:
•	When the restaurant is quiet, acknowledging and welcoming every guest is essential.
•	Service should be proactive, not reactive.
•	Food quality needs to reflect the promise of the cuisine—staples should

Pura Giri Natha Dili is Timor Leste’s largest Balinese Hindu temple, located in the Taibesi area on the southern outskirts of Dili. It was built in 1987 during the Indonesian administration for Balinese Hindu immigrants and Indonesian soldiers. The temple was inaugurated on June 27, 1987, by Governor Mário Viegas Carrascalão. After Timor Leste became independent in 1999, most Hindus left the country, and by 2015, only 272 Hindus were recorded in the national census. The temple later fell into serious disrepair and was also damaged during the violence in 1999 and the internal conflict in 2006.

Restoration of the temple is now underway. In 2021, the Timor Leste government allocated about US$1.2 million for its reconstruction, with additional support from the Udayana University Timor Leste Alumni Association. Lake Ira Lalaro is the largest lake in Timor-Leste. It is a seasonal body of water, whose size expands greatly during the wet season, from 1,000 hectares to 5,500 hectares. The northern shore is flat grassland that reclaims much of the lake during the dry season, while the southern shore is swampy with half drowned trees, more photogenic but harder to reach. It is hard is really appreciate the lake without using a drone as the landscape is so flat. The lake is apparently home to around 300 crocodiles, so be careful! Note that the road around the southern shore of the lake to Jaco Island is only passable by motorbike, and then only if you are comfortable driving over a rudimentary wooden bridge.

I have visited Atauro Island twice, first in 2025 and again in 2026, and every visit has reminded me why this island is considered one of the hidden jewels of the Coral Triangle.

It is encouraging to see Atauro recognized as one of the Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) within the Coral Triangle Marine Protected Area System (CTMPAS). It is also inspiring that the island is progressing toward the IUCN Green List, reflecting its commitment to effective and sustainable protected area management.
If you love nature, marine life, and authentic island experiences, Atauro Island is a destination that deserves a place on your travel list. I hope its unique ecosystems continue to be protected for future generations.

When Timor Leste was occupied by Indonesia, this beach was known as "Pantai pasir putih" in Bahasa Indonesia, or "White sand beach". The name is appropriate - although not particularly imaginative - as the beach is covered in white sand!

When I visited, some 23 years ago, the beach was quite eerie. It was deserted, apart from myself, and there were little concrete picnic shelters dotted along the beach that were slowly filling with drifting sand or become overgrown with trees. There were also some old, decrepit "pedalo" boats, little boats that you can pedal in calm water, that were half-buried in the sand. Clearly, the shelters and pedal-boats dated from the 1970s, some twenty years earlier, when East Timor was a Portuguese colony and a popular destination for Portuguese holiday-makers.

It would be interesting to know if any of the old, decrepit concrete picnic shelters, or any other trace of its old history, still remain.
It's a must go destination

Ramelau. He‘ll drop you at the place called „Fleixa“ about 8 km after Maubisse. There‘s a sign „Mt. Ramelau“ pointing to a very bad unpaved road on the right. If you walk on this road, it‘s 18 km to Hatu Builico. The road is very scenic. In my case I met a villager from Hatu Builico and I just walked with him. He used cow paths and walked in straight line from Fleixa to Hatu Builico. This reduces the distance and took me only 2 hours to reach Hatu Builico but I wouldn’t attempt this if I was alone.
